title: Sep 10 Results: Tough Night on the Mound
summary: Sep 10 predictions went 2-3 (40%) - breaking down what went wrong from the rubber

content.value:
## The Reality Check

Let me be straight with you - tonight was a grinder. Going 2-3 with a 40% hit rate isn't what we came here to do. As a former pitcher, I know what it's like when your command isn't there and batters are laying off your best stuff. That's essentially what happened with our model tonight. Three misses hurt, but let's break down the tape and see where we lost the zone.

## Game-by-Game Breakdown

From a pitcher's perspective, let's dissect each matchup and understand what the numbers missed versus what happened on the field.

## The Misses - Where We Lost Command

**Rays @ Braves (54% Rays)** - The Braves lineup came through when it mattered. Sometimes the home team's bats wake up, and you can't predict which inning they'll strike.

**Astros @ Phillies (50% Phillies)** - This was essentially a coin flip, and the coin didn't land our way. At 50%, we're talking about two evenly matched clubs, and the Astros proved why.

**Rangers @ Mariners (54% Rangers)** - Seattle's pitching likely shut down the Rangers' attack. Close confidence means close game, and we ended up on the wrong side.

## The Wins - What Worked

**Yankees (61%)** - Our highest confidence play delivered. The Rockies at Yankee Stadium is usually a mismatch, and the numbers held.

**Pirates (59%)** - Second-highest confidence, second win. When you trust your stuff and throw strikes, good things happen.

content.title: ⚠️ Tomorrow's Slate
content.sub: Off-day across MLB - time to review the tape and reset

content.value:
## The Film Session

Here's what I'm taking from tonight: our higher confidence picks (59%+) went 2-0. The three misses? All 54% or lower. That's the game telling us something. When you're working with marginal edges, variance catches up fast.

In the bullpen, we'd call this a session where your secondary pitches weren't fooling anyone. Your fastball worked (the high-confidence calls), but your changeup and slider got hammered (the close calls).

## Looking Ahead

With no games tomorrow, it's a perfect time to recalibrate. Every pitcher needs a bullpen day to work on mechanics. We'll use this off-day to dive deeper into what separated our hits from our misses.

The beauty of baseball? You get another chance to toe the rubber soon. We'll be sharper next time.

*- Ace*

author: Ace
